searchText: Thank you ser, skimmed it and just need to think about the naming convention, I was using capital letters to denote commitments and ignoring clippy. Though maybe it’s better to use lowercase and rely on the user using rust-analyser which shows the types I figured it was for mathematical notation to denote specific variables. I fixed it just because I was fixing clippy stuff in a spree, but I don’t have a preference either way, and can swap in back capital letters + clippy ignores on them if you want I did mean to ask you about some of the unused code which is blocking clippy CI being added back, is that leftover from previous versions or needed for future additions? You mean like the fuzzer code? Some structs have unread fields, and some variables are unused I’m working on adding fuzzer + benchmarks back in so I can add in async Ah I think some of those are from fields being used in tests only. One thing I think that we can get rid of is ‘verkle_db’ it was meant to be used so that consumers could provide a key value db and then all of the necessary verkle method would be automatically implemented, but I think that clients will probably need to do this themselves based on their internal infrastructure <@834543635587924028> saw your PR, I like the structure. Maybe I’m misreading it, are you suggesting to add “Topological Sorting” as a concrete item or was it an example for algorithms? Ok, do you mind if I break out tests into `/tests` folder as well, and delete `main.rs` (since rust-verkle is a lib)? Yeah main.rs can be removed. I’d prefer to keep unit tests in the same module and put integration tests in /tests Ok, then this would just be `trie_fuzzer` going into `/tests` then correct? Yeah exactly Ok, I can quickly add these to my PR shortly Sounds great, thank you ser Glad to help, changes are on my PR now. I can do whatever you want on the `C_1` vs `c_1` thing as well btw LGTM, we can use c_1 as in your PR. I think changes to those variable names might need to be first done at a higher level in docs, then propagated to implementations, so out of scope for this PR Should be merged now ser 🎉

excerpts.author: controlcthenv
excerpts.content: I figured it was for mathematical notation to denote specific variables. I fixed it just because I was fixing clippy stuff in a spree, but I don’t have a preference either way, and can swap in back capital letters + clippy ignores on them if you want

excerpts.author: controlcthenv

excerpts.content: You mean like the fuzzer code?

excerpts.author: controlcthenv
excerpts.content: Some structs have unread fields, and some variables are unused

excerpts.author: controlcthenv
excerpts.content: I’m working on adding fuzzer + benchmarks back in so I can add in async

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content:
Ah I think some of those are from fields being used in tests only.

One thing I think that we can get rid of is ‘verkle_db’ it was meant to be used so that consumers could provide a key value db and then all of the necessary verkle method would be automatically implemented, but I think that clients will probably need to do this themselves based on their internal infrastructure

excerpts.content: Yeah main.rs can be removed. I’d prefer to keep unit tests in the same module and put integration tests in /tests
